key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel.
engineering_relevance: The coating offers a promising route to improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of SA516 boiler components.
method: Apply Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The best-performing coating showed 95.71% lower weight gain than bare steel, with protection attributed to dense Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, NiTiO₄, and NiO scales, reduced porosity, and enhanced microhardness.
watch_item: Results cover 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles; long-term performance in corrosive boiler service remains unverified.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
